name: Crescent over Three Continents: The Ottoman Story
description: Six centuries of sultans, soldiers, architects and traders, from a frontier principality in Anatolia to an empire ruled from Istanbul, and finally the birth of modern Turkey.

checkpoints.name: From frontier to state
checkpoints.note: After Manzikert, Turkish clans entered Anatolia. A small Ottoman state grew near the weakened Byzantine Empire, formed the Janissaries, and survived defeat by Timur.

checkpoints.name: Constantinople
checkpoints.note: Mehmed II breached the walls of Constantinople and made it Istanbul. Hagia Sophia became a mosque, Topkapi Palace housed the court, and the Mamluks were soon beaten.

checkpoints.name: Suleiman's age
checkpoints.note: Suleiman the Magnificent made laws and led armies, Sinan designed mosques, and the Ottomans fought Safavid Persia. The navy lost at Lepanto in 1571, but the empire stayed strong.

checkpoints.name: Coffee, mosques and siege
checkpoints.note: The Sultan Ahmed Mosque was built and coffeehouses spread from Istanbul across Europe. The failed siege of Vienna in 1683 marked the limit of Ottoman advance.

checkpoints.name: The sick man of Europe
checkpoints.note: Greek independence and the Crimean War showed the empire's weakness, and reforms could not stop the slow loss of Balkan and Arab lands to new nations and powers.

checkpoints.name: Defeat and a new republic
checkpoints.note: After the First World War Mustafa Kemal Ataturk led resistance, the Treaty of Lausanne set borders, and Turkey became a republic in 1923, with a new capital at Ankara.
